[b]ERENE WORLD CUP 2028 MATCHDAY 8 GROUP STAGES![/b]

[Spoiler=Tirakan vs UREV]Tirakan came in knowing that victory would likely push them through the group with 6 points, and they played like a team that could already see the finish line. In the 28th minute, Beyilir opened the scoring with a moment of pure class, gliding past his marker before curling a beautiful shot into the far corner, the kind that makes the net ripple gently like its applauding. He doubled the lead in the 53rd, but this time there was nothing gentle about it. Tirakan broke forward at speed, the defense scrambling, and Beyilir smashed a first-time finish low into the net with ruthless precision. Two goals, two completely different moods, both deadly. UREV found a response in the 64th minute through Shinji, who pounced on a loose ball in the box and squeezed it through a forest of legs into the corner. It wasnt pretty, but it injected just enough tension to make Tirakan glance nervously at the clock. That tension didnt last. In the 79th minute, Lusuf stepped up and ended the conversation. Cutting in from the wing, he unleashed a long-range strike that swerved viciously before crashing into the top corner, a goal that didnt just restore control, it slammed the door shut. At full time, it finished 3-1, and with 6 points now in their hands, Tirakan are in a commanding position, all but set to advance from the group. One more step remains, but you can already feel them leaning into the next stage.

Tirakan 3 - 1 UREV
A. Beyilir 28',53'‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎I. Shinji  64'
I. Lusuf 79'

Match summary: https://freeimage.host/i/qCBGJ8N
[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Delareaux vs Eregovia]Eregovia walked onto the pitch with one clear intention, defend first, defend second, and maybe score if the universe allows it. They sat deep, lines compact, every player moving like part of a single machine, closing spaces until Delareaux looked like they were trying to play football in a crowded hallway. The breakthrough came through Palos, and it felt almost ironic. In the middle of all that defensive discipline, it was a sudden, clinical counter that struck first. Winning the ball in their own half, Eregovia surged forward with surprising speed, and Palos finished the move with a calm, composed strike into the bottom corner. One chance, one goal. Delareaux tried to respond, pushing numbers forward, but it only played into Eregovias hands. The more they attacked, the more space they left behind, and in the second half, Palos punished them again. Another break, another moment of precision, this time slotting the ball past the keeper with quiet confidence, doubling the lead without any unnecessary flair. From there, it was pure control. Eregovia shut the game down completely, suffocating every attack, clearing every cross, blocking every shot like their lives depended on it. 2-0. No chaos, no drama, just discipline. The kind of performance that doesnt just win games, it drains the hope out of the opponent minute by minute.

Delareaux 0 - 2 Eregovia
 ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ C. Palos 14',21'

Match summary: https://freeimage.host/i/qCBNTZB
[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Lamandica vs Wellassona]Lamandica came out blazing, all attack, all intent, throwing numbers forward and trying to overwhelm Wellassona early. It looked like a matter of time before theyd break through, waves of pressure crashing again and again. But in the 24th minute, Wellassona struck completely against the run of play. A quick transition caught Lamandica exposed, and Zima made them pay, finishing coolly with a low strike past the keeper. One chance, one goal, and suddenly the entire match tilted. From there, it turned into a siege. Lamandica dominated possession, probing, crossing, shooting, but Wellassona dug in with stubborn resilience. Every attack was met with a block, a clearance, or a last-ditch tackle, like a wall that kept rebuilding itself every time it cracked. As the minutes ticked away, frustration crept into Lamandicas play, their attacks growing more desperate, less precise. Meanwhile, Wellassona stayed disciplined, protecting their slim lead like it was gold. At full time, it ended 0-1. Not the louder team, not the flashier one, but the smarter and more patient side walked away with everything.

Lamandica 0 - 1 Wellassona
 ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  ‎  G. Zima  ‎ 24'

Match summary: https://freeimage.host/i/qCBvJSe
[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Jomsland vs Nevonia]Nevonia wasted no time, striking in just the 6th minute and silencing Jomsland early. A quick attacking move caught the defense off guard, and the finish was sharp and decisive, setting the tone before the match had even properly settled. But Jomsland didnt panic, they regrouped. By the 28th minute, Ragnarsson brought them back into it with a goal that felt like a reset button. Rising to meet a delivery into the box, he powered his finish past the keeper, shifting the momentum and waking the crowd. From there, the game tightened, both sides trading chances, but with a sense that Jomsland were slowly taking control. Nevonia tried to hold on, but the pressure kept building, minute by minute. Then in the 79th minute, Magnusson delivered the decisive moment. Timing his run perfectly, he latched onto a pass and finished with composure, placing the ball beyond the keeper to complete the turnaround. 2-1 to Jomsland. A match that began in chaos for them but ended in control, the kind of comeback that grows stronger with every passing minute.

Jomsland 2 - 1 Nevonia
S. Ragnarsson 28' W. Elgersma 6'
N. Magnusson 79'

[b]WVAA Launches 3 Flights in one Day[/b]
On Tuesday March 22, at 6:01 AM the first of three flight were launched, it was an unmanned Traja-IX rocket, the first to ever launch. It was carrying an empty Kal capsule (which is the one that will take Wesserns to the moon) into Erene orbit. An hour after it's launch, a Traja-I rocket carrying the first multi-crewed capsule launched (it was carrying two crew members). Due to it's success they had the capsule (which was capable of docking with other capsules) stay in orbit for longer so that the third and final rocket could launch, another Traja-I with two crew members. At 9:42 AM the mission known as Valmino-15 (the first Traja-I) docked with Valmino-16 (the second Traja-I). After 5 minutes the airlocks were finally opened and they shook hands with each other. They did multiple experiments before undocking. But when the two space crafts undocked disaster struck. Valmino-16 was sent into an uncontrollable spin, which resulted in the two people, Hoth Galithoi and Lily Dartinue (the second Wessern in space and the first female Wessern in space while on Valmino-14) Hoth was unable to move due to the fact that his arms had been pinned to his chair but Lily was able to move and reached for the controls. She quickly tried to stabilize the craft with the maneuvering thrusters but they had began spinning too fast and thus the only way to stop it was by using some of their lifeline, the boosters to help them get back into Erene orbit. She later remarked, "I could feel our fuel being wasted away by using the boosters to slow the spin." Luckily but her and Galithoi made it back safely. The public praises her quick thinking and saver her life and that of Galithois's. John Fredrickson awarded her the medal of Halithy (honor), the highest praise from the Council of 13.

After close inspection the WVAA found that one of the mini-explosives that were set to detonate and propel the capsules apart failed to go off, so now they are working on another version of undocking where small rockets will go off and, if one does not go off, all will stop so that the craft doesn't go into another uncontrollable spin.

The Traja-IX that had been launched that was safely returned to Erene and landed an hour before the two other spacecraft docked. Inside they found that there had been a panel that had come loose soon after reentry thus resulting in the capsule to sink, luckily they were able to recover it and most of the data, but now work is being done on the Kal capsule so that when we do launch people into space on the Kal capsule, they won't meet a watery end.
